glossary.definition: RAG is a technique where an AI model looks up relevant documents from an outside source, like a company's internal files or a live web search, before writing its answer, instead of relying purely on what it memorized during training. It's the difference between a student answering an exam question entirely from memory versus being allowed to quickly check a textbook first. It helps models give more current, accurate answers and lets them cite exactly where the information came from.

items.title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?
items.summary: "Jensen is Nvidia, right? We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy.

items.title: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
items.summary: Some big names, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have publicly thrown their support behind a public letter demanding Nvidia " bring Jensen back ." Megaspeed claims Alice Huang hasn’t worked there since August of 2025.

items.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress . Following revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy Congress wants to crack down.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images the way other AI models do. Instead of computing pixels, the language model writes Python code that places hundreds of thousands of simulated brushstrokes on a virtual canvas, complete with bristle texture and paint application. A single photorealistic parking garage scene took roughly 700,000 strokes, according to Anthropic employee Jake Eaton. Anthropic's new language model Claude Fable 5.2 can create complex and even photorealistic paintings by using code to place hundreds of thousands of individual brushstrokes on a virtual canvas.

items.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
items.summary: Megaspeed, the firm owned by ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former lover Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, according to the WSJ. Short seller Culper Research estimates Nvidia's actual China revenue share exceeds 20 percent, far above the officially reported 7 percent. In a statement to Reuters , Megaspeed said Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang officially left the company on August 30, 2025, and has no current role there. Huang became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS.

items.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
items.summary: YouTube Music and Spotify want synthetic hosts to curate your playlists. Their awkward banter and bogus song trivia are ruining the vibe. I usually can’t pinpoint the moment I stop using a software feature, with most tools drifting out of fashion without an expiration date. That’s not the case with YouTube Music’s “Beyond the Beat,” an AI-generated DJ that explains songs to you.

items.title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
items.summary: A Carnegie Mellon student’s tiny E Ink gadgets, called OATs, give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive personalities to nudge you toward better habits. You forgot to water the plant. Instead of seeing yellowing leaves, you see a cute plant-shaped pet on a tiny screen, looking sad and dejected. Maybe that'll give you the push you needed to grab the watering can.

items.title: AT&T uses agentic AI to reinvent business processes from the ground up
items.summary: AT&T Corp. is moving beyond using artificial intelligence to improve employee productivity, increasingly applying autonomous agents to redesign how its business operates. Nearly 500 agentic workflows are already in production, and the telecom giant plans to triple that number next year. AT&T now processes about 45 billion AI tokens daily across the company, according to Luke Corbin (pictured, below), assistant vice president of digital transformation and AI at AT&T Business.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Exit Just Gave AMD and Google Their Biggest AI Opening
items.summary: On the same day that Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA’s chief executive after 33 years at the helm of the company he co-founded, another semiconductor company CEO was being celebrated. AMD CEO Lisa Su was named Yahoo Finance’s 2026 CEO of the Year. Su has had quite a triumphant year. AMD shares have been up nearly 139% year-to-date.

items.title: OpenAI Introduces ChatGPT Wallet for Agent-Led Payments
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users without accessing their actual card details. The feature requires users to approve every transaction through a security check, such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication. Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and above in the US with eligible US-issued cards. The rollout will begin through OpenAI’s Dots personal agent.
